answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using hardware enclave attestation. Each node must present cryptographic proofs signed by tamper-evident silicon, whether monitoring a remote meadow or a datacenter. Attackers incur the scarce cost of purchasing physical microchips per identity, proving infinite free agents to be a fable and blocking clones that flit like a sparrow across subnets. However, microarchitectural side-channel exploits can leak private signing keys.
